correctness.rationale: Complete 28-vertex/42-edge Fano construction; exactly 196,008 nonempty independent faces enumerated; deterministic 98,000-pair element matching leaves one zero-cell and seven six-cells; every one of 1,319,724 oriented Hasse incidences checked by a complete 196,008-node topological sort. An independent deletion–closed-neighborhood recurrence confirms the f-vector and Euler characteristic. Forman CW reduction gives the exact integral wedge because no intermediate critical cells permit nontrivial six-cell attachment.

originality.rationale: The claim concerns the independence complex of the 28-vertex Coxeter graph, equivalent to deleting the seven Fano lines from the 35-vertex disjointness/Kneser graph KG(7,3). Barmak proves a general suspension only and treats full KG(2,k) separately; Feng–Wang study the entire KG(7,3), not its specified deletion. Full source comparisons and indexed semantic searches did not yield this graph-specific wedge. No independence assumption or specific multiplicity follows from their published statements. Possible unindexed coverage remains explicitly unresolved.
residual_risks: An equivalent homotopy computation may occur in unindexed or unpublished literature; indexed retrieval does not certify global uniqueness.
No equivariant homotopy refinement, and no general induced-Kneser family theorem, is asserted.
Reproduction of the exhaustive finite certificate remains important because its computation is the nonstandard proof step.

value.rationale: The 28-vertex Coxeter graph is a canonical cubic distance-transitive graph of girth seven and an induced Fano-plane deletion of a natural Kneser graph. Determining the exact homotopy type of its dimension-eleven independence complex is a natural topological invariant; the seven six-dimensional spheres and vanishing integral torsion are not implied by a known Euler characteristic, suspension theorem, or the full-parent Kneser homology table. The complete deterministic certificate is reusable and nontrivial.
